en: The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika), The Triplet of the Corrupt (Saṅkiliṭṭhattika)

Dependent on an unwholesome, defiled, and corrupting state, there arises a state that is neither unwholesome nor defiled and corrupting by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Three for root; three for predominance … pe … three for non-disappearance.

Dependent on an indeterminate, undefiled, and corrupting state, there arises a state that is neither indeterminate nor undefiled and corrupting by way of root-condition. Dependent on an indeterminate, undefiled, and corrupting state … [and so forth].
A state that is neither unwholesome nor afflicted-and-defiling arises by way of root-condition.
Conditioned by a state that is indeterminate, non-afflicted, yet defiling, a state that is neither unwholesome nor afflicted-and-defiling arises by way of root-condition.
Conditioned by a state that is indeterminate, non-afflicted, yet defiling, [a state that is] neither unwholesome nor afflicted-and-defiling...

Conditioned by a neutral (avyākata) phenomenon that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement (asaṅkiliṭṭha-asaṅkilesika), there arise phenomena that are neither unwholesome nor subject to defilement, as well as phenomena that are neutral and neither defiled nor subject to defilement, by way of the root condition (hetu-paccaya).

Conditioned by a neutral phenomenon that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement, there arise phenomena that are neither unwholesome nor subject to defilement, as well as phenomena that are neutral and neither defiled nor subject to defilement, by way of the root condition. [Conditioned by] a neutral phenomenon that is neither defiled nor subject to defilement...
Conditioned by a state that is neither unwholesome nor afflicted-and-defiled, there arise states that are neither unwholesome nor afflicted-and-defiled through the root-condition.

(Abbreviated. Under the root-condition there are six; under the object-condition there are six … [and so on] … under the repetition-condition there are five … [and so on] … under the resultant-condition there are three; under the non-disappearance-condition there are six.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is not corrupt and not subject to corruption, a state that is neither wholesome nor not corrupt and not subject to corruption arises by way of root condition … three.

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is not corrupt and not subject to corruption, a state that is neither wholesome nor not corrupt and not subject to corruption arises by way of root condition … three. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are six; under predominance condition there are six … pe … under result condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are six.
